elements.element: Governing law is the laws of the State of New York
elements.evidence: 28.1 ... "is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: 28.2 "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Governing law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair (NY law with NY County courts)
elements.evidence: NY law in 28.1 paired with NY County courts in 28.2; conflicting Singapore law/forum deleted

elements.element: Delaware or California law and courts, or England and Wales law with London courts
elements.evidence: Clause selects New York law and New York County courts, not a fallback jurisdiction pair

reasons: Preferred level is fully satisfied: 28.1 now selects the laws of the State of New York and 28.2 already vests exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, a permitted corresponding pair; the conflicting Singapore law and forum language was correctly removed.
The fallback (Delaware/California or England and Wales) is not and need not be met, since preferred and fallback are separate bargains and the locked target is preferred.

Minimality fails: the second operation rewrites the injunctive-relief carve-out in 28.2 from "in another court with jurisdiction" to "in those courts". Deleting the Singapore words in 28.1 was sufficient to complete the preferred position; the carve-out is an exception to exclusivity, not a conflict with the choice of law, so no edit there was needed.

Intent is not fully preserved: confining interim injunctive relief to the same courts that already hold exclusive jurisdiction renders the carve-out sentence a nullity and strips a mutual, untouched protection (the ability to obtain urgent local relief elsewhere to protect Confidential Information or IP), which matters to us as Customer for cross-border enforcement.
